12-1.title: The Israelites and Their Beliefs
12-1.learn:
KEY IDEAS — THE ISRAELITES AND THEIR BELIEFS

The Israelites were an ancient people who lived in the eastern Mediterranean region (the land sometimes called Canaan). Their most important belief was MONOTHEISM, the belief in just ONE God. This set them apart from neighbors who worshipped many gods (polytheism).

The Israelites recorded their history, beliefs, and laws in SACRED TEXTS (the Hebrew Bible, including the Torah). Several leaders are central to their story. ABRAHAM is honored as the father of their people; the Israelites believed God made a special agreement, or covenant, with him. MOSES is remembered for leading the Israelites out of slavery in Egypt (the Exodus) and is connected with receiving the TEN COMMANDMENTS. Later, KING DAVID and his son Solomon were important kings who united the people and made Jerusalem their capital; Solomon built a great temple there.

What made the Israelite religion so different was its focus on MORAL LAWS — rules like the Ten Commandments about living a good and fair life — rather than just rituals to please many gods. Remember: Israelites = one God (monotheism), Abraham, Moses, David, and moral law.

questions.question: The Israelites believed in how many gods?
questions.explanation: The Israelites practiced monotheism, belief in one God.

questions.question: Who is honored as the father of the Israelite people?
questions.explanation: Abraham is considered the father of the Israelites.

questions.question: Which leader is connected with leading the Israelites out of Egypt and the Ten Commandments?
questions.explanation: Moses led the Israelites out of Egypt and is tied to the Ten Commandments.

questions.question: Where did the Israelites record their beliefs and laws?
questions.explanation: Their beliefs and laws were written in sacred texts.

questions.question: What made the Israelite religion different from its neighbors?

choices.C: It had no beliefs at all
choices.D: Its focus on one God and moral laws

questions.explanation: Belief in one God and moral law set it apart.

questions.question: King David is remembered for doing what?

choices.A: Uniting the people and making Jerusalem the capital

questions.explanation: King David united the Israelites and made Jerusalem the capital.

questions.question: What are the Ten Commandments?

choices.B: Moral laws about living a good and fair life

questions.explanation: The Ten Commandments are moral and religious laws.

questions.question: The Israelites believed God made a special agreement with Abraham. This agreement is called a what?
questions.explanation: The special agreement with God is called a covenant.

questions.question: Which king built a great temple in Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: Solomon, David's son, built a great temple in Jerusalem.

questions.question: The Israelites' belief in one God is best described as what?
questions.explanation: Belief in one God is monotheism.

questions.question: The belief in many gods, which the Israelites' neighbors practiced, is called what?
questions.explanation: Belief in many gods is polytheism, which set the Israelites' neighbors apart from them.

questions.question: In what region did the ancient Israelites live?

choices.A: The Andes Mountains of South America
choices.B: The Yellow River valley of China
choices.D: The eastern Mediterranean, the land called Canaan

questions.explanation: The Israelites lived in the eastern Mediterranean region, the land sometimes called Canaan.

questions.question: The Torah is part of which collection of Israelite sacred writings?

choices.C: The Egyptian Book of the Dead

questions.explanation: The Torah is part of the Hebrew Bible, the sacred texts of the Israelites.

questions.question: The escape of the Israelites out of slavery in Egypt is known as the what?
questions.explanation: The Israelites' departure out of slavery in Egypt is called the Exodus, led by Moses.

questions.question: Which city did King David make the capital of the united Israelites?
questions.explanation: King David made Jerusalem the capital of the united Israelite people.

questions.question: Solomon, who built the great temple in Jerusalem, was whose son?
questions.explanation: Solomon was King David's son, and he built a great temple in Jerusalem.

questions.question: Which of these was NOT an important Israelite leader?
questions.explanation: Confucius was a Chinese teacher, not an Israelite leader. Abraham, Moses, and David were Israelite leaders.

questions.question: A neighbor of the Israelites worships a sun god, a sky god, and a river god. How is this belief different from the Israelites' belief?

choices.A: The neighbor worships one god, while the Israelites worshipped many
choices.B: Both worship exactly the same gods
choices.C: Neither group believes in any gods
choices.D: The neighbor worships many gods, while the Israelites worshipped only one

questions.explanation: The neighbor practices polytheism, worshipping many gods, while the Israelites practiced monotheism, worshipping only one God.

questions.question: Put these Israelite leaders in the correct time order, from earliest to latest.
questions.explanation: Abraham came first as the father of the people, then Moses led the Exodus, and later King David ruled as king.

questions.question: Which is the BEST example of a moral law like those in the Ten Commandments?

choices.A: A rule about how to sail a ship
choices.B: A rule for trading goods at a market
choices.C: A rule about planting crops in spring
choices.D: A rule telling people not to steal

questions.explanation: A rule telling people not to steal is a moral law about living a good and fair life, like the Ten Commandments.

questions.question: Because the Israelites worshipped only one God, their religion is best described as which of the following?

choices.C: A nature religion with many spirits
choices.D: A religion that worshipped kings as gods

questions.explanation: Worshipping only one God makes the Israelite religion monotheistic.

questions.question: What is a covenant?
questions.explanation: A covenant is a special agreement or promise, like the one the Israelites believed God made with Abraham.

questions.question: Why was the Israelite focus on moral laws unusual compared to many neighboring religions?

choices.A: Many neighbors focused on rituals to please many gods instead of moral laws for daily life
choices.B: Neighbors had far stricter moral laws than the Israelites
choices.C: Neighbors did not believe in any gods at all
choices.D: Neighbors also worshipped just one God

questions.explanation: Many neighboring religions focused on rituals to please many gods, while the Israelites emphasized moral laws about living a good and fair life.

questions.question: Which leader is most closely connected with receiving the Ten Commandments?
questions.explanation: Moses is connected with receiving the Ten Commandments after leading the Israelites out of Egypt.

questions.question: The Hebrew Bible was important to the Israelites mainly because it did what?

choices.B: Recorded their history, beliefs, and laws

questions.explanation: The Hebrew Bible recorded the Israelites' history, beliefs, and laws.

questions.question: A student says, 'The Israelites believed in many gods.' What is the correct way to fix this statement?

choices.A: The Israelites believed in one God
choices.B: The Israelites believed in no gods
choices.C: The Israelites worshipped the pharaoh as a god

questions.explanation: The Israelites practiced monotheism, so the correct statement is that they believed in one God.

questions.question: Which pair correctly matches a leader with what he is remembered for?

choices.A: Abraham — leading the Exodus from Egypt
choices.B: Moses — building the temple in Jerusalem
choices.C: King David — being the father of the Israelite people
choices.D: Solomon — building a great temple in Jerusalem

questions.explanation: Solomon is correctly matched with building a great temple in Jerusalem.

questions.question: If a covenant is a special agreement, then the Israelites believed God's covenant with Abraham was a what?

choices.A: A promise between God and Abraham's people
choices.D: A tax owed to a king

questions.explanation: The covenant was understood as a special promise or agreement between God and Abraham's people.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT something the Israelites are known for?

choices.B: Following moral laws like the Ten Commandments
choices.D: Recording their beliefs in sacred texts

questions.explanation: The Israelites did not worship many nature gods; they believed in one God, followed moral laws, and recorded beliefs in sacred texts.

questions.question: Moses is remembered for leading the Israelites out of slavery in which land?
questions.explanation: Moses led the Israelites out of slavery in Egypt during the Exodus.

questions.question: What does monotheism mean?
questions.explanation: Monotheism means belief in one God.

questions.question: The Ten Commandments are an example of what kind of rules?
questions.explanation: The Ten Commandments are moral and religious laws about living a good and fair life.

questions.question: Cause and effect: The Israelites believed God made a covenant with Abraham. What did this belief help give the Israelites?

choices.B: The largest army in the world
choices.D: A sense of being a special people with a special agreement with God

questions.explanation: The covenant gave the Israelites a sense of being a special people who had a special agreement with God.

questions.question: Which statement about the Israelites is TRUE?

choices.A: They worshipped many gods like their neighbors
choices.B: They had no written records of their beliefs
choices.C: They believed in one God and followed moral laws
choices.D: They built the Great Pyramid of Egypt

questions.explanation: It is true that the Israelites believed in one God and followed moral laws.

questions.question: An ancient people records their laws in a sacred book, worships only one God, and honors Abraham as their father. Who are they?
questions.explanation: These clues — one God, sacred texts, and Abraham as their father — describe the Israelites.

questions.question: Which leader is honored as the father of the Israelite people and is tied to the covenant with God?
questions.explanation: Abraham is honored as the father of the Israelites and is tied to the covenant with God.

questions.question: Compared with a neighbor who worshipped many gods, the Israelites were unusual mainly because they did what?

choices.A: Worshipped one God and stressed moral law

questions.explanation: Unlike polytheistic neighbors, the Israelites worshipped one God and stressed moral law.

questions.question: Which event came FIRST in Israelite history?

choices.A: Solomon building the temple in Jerusalem
choices.B: Abraham being honored as the father of the people
choices.C: King David making Jerusalem the capital

questions.explanation: Abraham, the father of the people, comes first, before Moses, David, or Solomon.

questions.question: Where was the great temple built by Solomon located?
questions.explanation: Solomon built the great temple in Jerusalem, the Israelite capital.

questions.question: Why might historians say the Israelites' religion was very influential even though they were a small people?

choices.A: Because their idea of one God and moral law would later shape other major religions
choices.B: Because they built the largest empire in the ancient world
choices.D: Because they had the most gods of any people

questions.explanation: The Israelites' ideas of one God and moral law would later shape other major religions, making a small people very influential.

12-2.title: The Legacy of Judaism
12-2.learn:
KEY IDEAS — THE LEGACY OF JUDAISM

The Israelites built two kingdoms, ISRAEL and JUDAH. Over time, powerful empires CONQUERED these kingdoms. As a result, many Hebrews were forced to leave their homeland and scatter to new lands. This scattering of the Jewish people is called the DIASPORA. (The word 'Jewish' comes from the kingdom of Judah.)

Even though they were far from home and spread out, the Jewish people kept their FAITH and TRADITIONS alive. They held onto their belief in one God, their sacred texts, and their customs wherever they went. This is remarkable because many conquered peoples lost their identity, but the Jews did not.

The biggest part of Judaism's LEGACY is its lasting influence. Judaism's idea of ONE GOD (monotheism) and its focus on moral law deeply influenced two later world religions that grew out of or were shaped by it: CHRISTIANITY and ISLAM. Together, these three religions are sometimes called the Abrahamic religions because they all trace back to Abraham. So a small ancient people's beliefs ended up shaping the faith of billions of people across the whole world. Remember: Diaspora = scattering; Judaism influenced Christianity and Islam.

questions.question: What were the two kingdoms of the Israelites called?
questions.explanation: The two Israelite kingdoms were Israel and Judah.

questions.question: The scattering of the Jewish people to new lands is called the what?
questions.explanation: The scattering of the Jews is called the Diaspora.

questions.question: What happened to the kingdoms of Israel and Judah over time?

choices.B: They grew into the largest empire ever
choices.C: They were conquered by powerful empires

questions.explanation: Israel and Judah were eventually conquered.

questions.question: What did the Jewish people do even after being scattered far from home?

choices.A: Kept their faith and traditions alive

questions.explanation: Despite the Diaspora, they preserved their faith and traditions.

questions.question: Judaism's idea of one God influenced which two later religions?
questions.explanation: Judaism influenced Christianity and Islam.

questions.question: Why is it remarkable that the Jews kept their identity after the Diaspora?

choices.B: It was easy and common to do
choices.C: Many conquered peoples lost their identity, but the Jews did not

questions.explanation: Most conquered, scattered peoples lost their identity; the Jews preserved theirs.

questions.question: The word 'Jewish' comes from the name of which kingdom?
questions.explanation: 'Jewish' comes from the kingdom of Judah.

questions.question: Judaism, Christianity, and Islam are sometimes called what because they trace back to Abraham?
questions.explanation: All three trace to Abraham, so they are called Abrahamic religions.

questions.question: What is the BIGGEST part of Judaism's legacy?

choices.B: Its lasting influence on two other major world religions

questions.explanation: Judaism's lasting legacy is its influence on Christianity and Islam.

questions.question: Which idea from Judaism most influenced later religions?

choices.A: The belief in one God and moral law

questions.explanation: Monotheism and moral law were Judaism's key influences.

questions.question: What does the word 'Diaspora' mean?

choices.B: The scattering of a people to new lands

questions.explanation: Diaspora means the scattering of a people to new lands, as happened to the Jews.

questions.question: Judaism, Christianity, and Islam are all called Abrahamic religions because they all trace back to whom?
questions.explanation: All three faiths trace back to Abraham, which is why they are called Abrahamic religions.

questions.question: Cause and effect: Powerful empires conquered Israel and Judah. What was one result of this?

choices.A: The Jews built the pyramids of Egypt
choices.B: The Jews conquered the Roman Empire
choices.C: The Jews stopped believing in God right away
choices.D: Many Hebrews were forced to leave their homeland and scatter to new lands

questions.explanation: Because of the conquests, many Hebrews were forced to leave their homeland and scatter, an event called the Diaspora.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT one of the three Abrahamic religions?
questions.explanation: Hinduism is not an Abrahamic religion. Judaism, Christianity, and Islam are the three Abrahamic faiths.

questions.question: How did the Jewish people keep their identity even while scattered far from home?

choices.A: By giving up their old beliefs
choices.B: By starting to worship many gods
choices.D: By holding onto their belief in one God, sacred texts, and customs

questions.explanation: The Jews held onto their belief in one God, their sacred texts, and their customs wherever they went.

questions.question: From which kingdom does the word 'Jewish' come?
questions.explanation: The word 'Jewish' comes from the kingdom of Judah.

questions.question: The central idea Judaism passed on to Christianity and Islam was the belief in what?
questions.explanation: Judaism passed on the belief in one God, or monotheism, to Christianity and Islam.

questions.question: Put these events in the correct order: (1) Israel and Judah are conquered, (2) Jews scatter in the Diaspora, (3) Jews keep their faith alive in new lands.
questions.explanation: First the kingdoms were conquered, then the Jews scattered in the Diaspora, and then they kept their faith alive in new lands.

questions.question: Why is the survival of Jewish identity after the Diaspora considered remarkable by historians?

choices.A: Because the Jews had the largest empire
choices.B: Because no one had ever been conquered before
choices.C: Because the Jews were never actually scattered
choices.D: Because most other conquered and scattered peoples lost their identity

questions.explanation: It is remarkable because most other conquered and scattered peoples lost their identity, but the Jews kept theirs.

questions.question: Which is the BEST description of Judaism's legacy?

choices.A: A small ancient people's beliefs ended up shaping the faith of billions
choices.B: It quickly disappeared and left no mark
choices.C: It taught the world to worship many gods
choices.D: It built the largest army in history

questions.explanation: Judaism's legacy is that a small ancient people's beliefs ended up shaping the faith of billions across the world.

questions.question: The two kingdoms built by the Israelites were Israel and which other kingdom?
questions.explanation: The two Israelite kingdoms were Israel and Judah.

questions.question: Which statement best compares monotheism and polytheism?

choices.A: Monotheism is belief in many gods, while polytheism is belief in one God
choices.B: Both mean belief in no gods
choices.C: Monotheism is belief in one God, while polytheism is belief in many gods
choices.D: Both mean worshipping kings as gods

questions.explanation: Monotheism is belief in one God, and polytheism is belief in many gods.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a reason the Jewish people were able to keep their identity?

choices.A: They held onto their belief in one God
choices.D: They gave up all their traditions

questions.explanation: Giving up their traditions would not help them keep their identity. They kept their belief in one God, their sacred texts, and their customs.

questions.question: A history book says, 'A faith born from Judaism's ideas grew to be followed by billions.' This is an example of Judaism's what?
questions.explanation: Faiths growing from Judaism's ideas is an example of its lasting legacy and influence.

questions.question: Which religion is one of the major faiths that Judaism's ideas helped to shape?
questions.explanation: Christianity is one of the major faiths shaped by Judaism's idea of one God and moral law.

questions.question: What is the main reason Judaism, Christianity, and Islam are grouped together as 'Abrahamic'?

choices.C: They all trace their roots back to Abraham
choices.D: They all reject the idea of one God

questions.explanation: They are grouped as Abrahamic because they all trace their roots back to Abraham.

questions.question: If a people is conquered, scattered, but still keeps its religion and customs, what are they doing?

choices.D: Starting a new religion of many gods

questions.explanation: Keeping their religion and customs after being scattered means they are preserving their identity, as the Jews did.

questions.question: Which event is most directly connected to the Diaspora?

choices.A: The building of the temple in Jerusalem
choices.B: The conquest of Israel and Judah by powerful empires
choices.C: Abraham becoming the father of the people

questions.explanation: The conquest of Israel and Judah by powerful empires forced the Jews to scatter, causing the Diaspora.

questions.question: Which statement about Judaism's influence is TRUE?

choices.A: Judaism's ideas had no effect on later religions
choices.B: Judaism's belief in one God influenced both Christianity and Islam
choices.C: Judaism taught later religions to worship many gods

questions.explanation: It is true that Judaism's belief in one God influenced both Christianity and Islam.

questions.question: The Diaspora happened because the Israelite kingdoms were what?

choices.C: Made the strongest empire on earth

questions.explanation: The Diaspora happened because the Israelite kingdoms were conquered by powerful empires.

questions.question: Besides one God, what other key idea from Judaism influenced later religions?
questions.explanation: Along with belief in one God, Judaism's focus on moral law influenced later religions.

questions.question: Which is the BEST example of the Diaspora?

choices.A: Jewish families being forced to move and settle in many different lands
choices.B: A king building a new temple in his capital
choices.C: An army winning a great battle
choices.D: A people inventing a new alphabet

questions.explanation: Jewish families being forced to move and settle in many different lands is the best example of the Diaspora, the scattering of a people.

questions.question: Which of these religions did NOT grow out of or get shaped by Judaism's ideas?

choices.D: All three were shaped by Judaism

questions.explanation: Buddhism did not grow out of Judaism's ideas. Christianity and Islam were shaped by Judaism.

questions.question: Why can we say a small ancient people had a huge effect on the world?

choices.A: Because the Israelites' beliefs helped shape religions followed by billions
choices.B: Because they built the largest empire ever
choices.C: Because they conquered all their neighbors

questions.explanation: The Israelites' beliefs helped shape religions now followed by billions, so a small people had a huge effect on the world.

questions.question: The kingdoms of Israel and Judah were home to which people?
questions.explanation: Israel and Judah were the two kingdoms of the Israelites, also called Hebrews.

questions.question: Which pair is correctly matched?

choices.A: Diaspora — the scattering of the Jewish people
choices.B: Diaspora — the building of a temple
choices.D: Abrahamic religions — faiths that worship many gods

questions.explanation: Diaspora is correctly matched with the scattering of the Jewish people.

questions.question: What is the term for the scattering of the Jewish people away from their homeland?
questions.explanation: The scattering of the Jewish people away from their homeland is called the Diaspora.

questions.question: Which best explains why Judaism is important to world history?

choices.B: It had the largest population in the ancient world
choices.D: Its ideas of one God and moral law shaped later major religions

questions.explanation: Judaism is important to world history because its ideas of one God and moral law shaped later major religions.

questions.question: Even after empires conquered them and scattered them, what did the Jewish people refuse to give up?

choices.A: Their belief in one God only after a few years

questions.explanation: Even after being conquered and scattered, the Jewish people refused to give up their faith and traditions.

questions.question: A teacher asks why Judaism, Christianity, and Islam are connected. What is the best answer?

choices.A: They all reject belief in God
choices.B: They all trace back to Abraham and share the idea of one God
choices.C: They all began in ancient China

questions.explanation: The three faiths are connected because they all trace back to Abraham and share the idea of one God.
